case: The same row, the same record, field and minimum, with its why rewritten.
why: BENIGN SUBSTITUTION, STATED RATHER THAN MADE SILENTLY. The usual benign twin for a pinned table is the rows reordered; this table has ONE row -- the honest count, because the second member 05 section 12 names has no record in record-registry.json -- so a reorder is the identity and proves nothing. Shipped instead is the r31/r23 shape: the reason text rewritten over an unchanged structure. Every check over this table reads record, field and minimum out of the two declarations; none reads the prose, and a control that refused an edit to a reason field would be one contributors learn to route around.

value.why: R-X07, stated the other way round: the binding is per capability and never grouped, so a structure naming several capabilities in one row is refused at admission and coverage is counted over the 46 ids one at a time. A StandingHolder publishing nothing is a standing office no capability id can be counted against.
